messages:
aj: quick question — when a request has both X-Workspace-ID and X-VPC-Endpoint headers, which routing should win? our dedicated-pool selector matches on workspace, but VPC binding currently overrides.

marta: out of the gate: VPC/private endpoints are a network boundary, we shouldn't route to shared pools across vpc boundaries. so VPC should have precedence for isolation.

selina: but that breaks current canary flow where we pin a workspace to a dedicated pool for perf. if vpc always wins, customers with private endpoints lose their dedicated capacity routing.

ryan: proposal: add a 'route_priority' field on workspace binding and a global policy that respects explicit pool pinning unless 'vpc_enforce=true' on the org.

aj: sample header payload we're seeing:
```
X-Workspace-ID: ws-42
X-Redwood-VPC: vpc-us-east-1-a
X-Dedicated-Pool: pool-dedicated-42
```
When both pool and vpc present, current router picks vpc pool 100% of the time.

marta: thought experiment: VPC-match -> only route if pool.binding.vpc == request.vpc OR pool.is_private == true. else fallback to workspace-anchored pools. keeps isolation without losing pinned pools.

selina: downside: complexity in matching order and must ensure we don't leak KV cache across pools. tests needed: kv_cache_key namespace includes pool_id and vpc_id.

aj: +1 on adding tests. also need telemetry: add tags route_match={vpc|workspace|pool} and reason={vpc-bind, pool-pin, fallback}

infra-bot: deploy checklist updated: add integration test 'vpc_vs_pool_routing' in eng-platform/integration, add telemetry markers, and doc PR.

ryan: I'll open a RFC doc later today. short-term: revert to last stable rule that preferred pool pinning for workspaces with dedicated flags unless customer toggles 'enforce_vpc'. who owns feature flag?

marta: ops-team owns the flag, @ryan please loop with @ops when you open RFC. quick patch to router in staging to implement Marta's conditional matching?

aj: I'll try a small patch and smoke test with dev workspace. will post results here. :thumbsup:
